<details>
The PKGBUILD is straightforward. The global/top-level scope contains only plain variable assignments (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `provides`, `conflicts`, `optdepends`, `source`, `source_x86_64`, `source_aarch64`, and the `sha256sums*` arrays). There are no command substitutions, no `eval`, no `base64` decoding, no network fetches, and no file operations executed at source time. Nothing runs when `makepkg --printsrcinfo` sources this file.

The `source*` arrays point to the project's own upstream GitHub repository/release assets (raw.githubusercontent.com and github.com/rylos/rynas), which is expected for this package. Checksums are actually provided for all three artifacts (not SKIP), so the sources are pinned. The only function body, `package()`, merely installs the prebuilt binary and the service unit into `$pkgdir`; it does not run during `--printsrcinfo` and contains nothing suspicious anyway.

No malicious behavior is present in the executed scope of this command.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Only static variable assignments at top level; nothing executes during printsrcinfo.</summary>
</security_assessment>
